subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Alicia / Tom 

Thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap so we all have the same next steps and success criteria. Appreciate you walking us through Acme's current setup.

Pain points we heard:
- Inconsistent structured outputs from current agent workflows (payloads vary by integrator).
- Hard to enforce deterministic formatting for downstream parsers (missing fields / type drift).
- Latency spikes during batch jobs when using function-calling hooks.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Backend: Node.js microservices (Koa) behind Kubernetes
- Orchestration: internal agent that calls 3rd-party tools (CRM, billing) via HTTP webhooks
- Models: mix of hosted LLMs + local smaller models for deterministic tasks

Success criteria (from our discussion):
1) Agent responses must validate against a single JSON schema with strict types (no free-text where JSON expected).
2) 95%+ of responses match schema on first pass (determinism), with clear fallback behavior for non-matching outputs.
3) End-to-end latency for tool-calling sequence < 700ms median for simple flows.
4) Easy rollout to production: sandbox → canary → prod with observability for regressions.

What Redwood recommends (high level):
- Define a strict JSON schema for all agent tool outputs and enforce it at the runtime layer (we can attach a sample below).
- Use deterministic temperature/decoding settings for tool-calling prompts and validate the asserted schema before committing to the downstream system.
- Add a validation + auto-corrections step (small deterministic parser) as a fall-through for non-critical mismatches.

Next steps / action items:
- Redwood to share a reference schema (attached: acme-schema-v1.json) and a short demo showing schema validation + auto-correct flow (Jordan to schedule).
- Acme to confirm the list of critical fields and a representative prompt set for 10 example workflows (Alicia).
- Plan a technical deep-dive with your integration engineer (Tom) — propose Wed/Thu next week.

Attachments: 20260625-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), acme-schema-v1.json (reference schema draft).

If I've missed anything, please flag. Happy to iterate the schema quickly.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 17:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Thanks Jordan  this captures the call well. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the "95%+ match" should be measured against our existing dataset of 2k runs, not just the example prompts. We'll share a sample export.
- Latency: 700ms median is reasonable for the simple flows you mentioned; for multi-step tool chains we expect median < 1.2s.
- Stakeholders: adding Procurement (cc'd Tom) for timeline/contract questions and our Platform Eng lead (not on thread yet) for the deep technical review.

Two asks from Acme: 
1) Can you include an example of the runtime validation failure mode (what the SDK/runtime does when a response fails schema validation)? Example: return a structured error + raw output for logging.
2) Please confirm whether Redwood's runtime will allow us to pin a deterministic model config per route (temperature, top_p, decoding).

I'll pull together the 10 representative workflows and a dataset export by EOD Monday.
